title: Term Life Insurance Rate Manual: The Waiver Removal Reckoning
content:
When the waiver of premium rider of a Term Life Insurance policy ends at the anniversary on which the insured's anniversary age reaches the product's waiver rider expiry age, the installment after the waiver rider ends is the installment premium on record with the waiver charge taken out. The waiver removal reckoning works it out as follows.

**Ages.** The insured's issue age is the whole years from the insured's date of birth to the issue date on record; the insured's anniversary age is the whole years from the insured's date of birth to the most recent policy anniversary on or before today.

**Face premium.** The band measurement face is the face amount on record alone and the band factor is 1.00. The face premium is the face amount on record divided by 1,000, times the rate per 1,000 on record, times the band factor, rounded to the cent.

**Accidental death charge.** The accidental death rider rate is 1.08 per 1,000 when the insured's anniversary age is from 60 through 69 (60 or more and below 70), 0.84 per 1,000 when it is below 45, and the product's accidental death rider rate per 1,000 at any other age. The accidental death charge is the accidental death rider amount on record divided by 1,000, times that rate, rounded to the cent.

**Children's term charge.** The unit rate is 5.00 when 11 or more units are on record, 5.50 when 5 through 10 units are on record, and the product's children's term rate per unit below 5 units; the charge is the units on record times the unit rate.

**Waiver charge.** The waiver rate is 0.11 and the waiver charge base is the face premium alone. When the waiver of premium rider is attached on record, the waiver charge is the waiver rate times the waiver charge base, rounded to the cent; when it is not attached there is no waiver charge.

**Modal factor.** That of the premium mode on record: the product's quarterly factor for quarterly, monthly bank-draft factor for monthly bank draft, semiannual factor for semiannual and annual factor for annual.

**Result.** The waiver charge removed when the rider ends is the waiver rate times the waiver charge base, rounded to the cent; its installment share is that charge times the modal factor of the premium mode on record, rounded to the cent. The installment after the waiver rider ends is the installment premium on record less the installment share of the waiver charge removed, rounded to the cent.

Nothing else is taken out of the installment on record: the policy fee it carries is left as it stands, whatever fee before sharing (the product's annual policy fee, or that fee less 10.00 for a face below 250000 or less 20.00 for a face of 1000000 or more), long-standing fee concession (10.00 or 5.00) or policy fee share (the whole, one half (0.5) or none of the fee) it reflects; the accidental death and children's term charges likewise stay in it.

### Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Face on record | 400000 |
| Rate per 1,000 on record | 2.50 |
| Mode on record | quarterly |
| Installment premium on record | 320.15 |

Face premium: 400 times 2.50 times 1.00, which is 1000.00. Waiver charge removed: 0.11 times 1000.00, which is 110.00. Installment share: 110.00 times 0.265, which is 29.15. Installment after the waiver rider ends: 320.15 less 29.15, which is 291.00.

The same policy in semiannual mode with an installment on record of 628.10 gives an installment share of 110.00 times 0.52, which is 57.20, and an installment after the waiver rider ends of 570.90.
